newsitem.title: UK: Irish minister says N.Ireland "extremely tense".
newsitem.headline: Irish minister says N.Ireland "extremely tense".

text.p: Irish deputy prime minister Dick Spring said on Sunday that Northern Ireland is "extremely tense" amid growing IRA guerrilla violence and a spate of sectarian arson attacks.

Spring, one of the architects of an Anglo-Irish peace drive which stalled after the Irish Republican Army abandoned a truce last year, called on the guerrillas to end hostilities and win a voice in peace talks.

"The situation is, I would say, extremely tense, given the places of worship being burnt on both sides, the attempted (killing) of the constable and also the attitude being taken by hardline Unionists (pro-British Protestants) in relation to the marching season," he said.
There have recently been attacks on British forces, rival church burnings and uncertainty about summer parades by Protestants that last year triggered violence.

As Spring spoke on Irish radio, police questioned seven men from the hardline republican South Armagh area after British forces captured a powerful IRA sniper gun and clearing up went on in a Belfast flashpoint after Protestant and Catholic clashes.
A policewoman was still seriously ill on Sunday after being shot by an IRA sniper in Northern Ireland's second city, Londonderry, last Thursday.
If the IRA continued to wage war against British rule then the result would be the continued exclusion of its Sinn Fein political arm from multi-party talks, Spring said.
The Anglo-Irish discussions, chaired by former U.S. senator George Mitchell, adjourned in deadlock recently to allow parties to prepare for Britain's May 1 election.

Security forces found a U.S.-made Barrett .50 "Light Fifty" rifle, one of the IRA's most prized weapons, in a raid aimed at tracking down arms used by snipers who have killed 11 soldiers and police since 1992.
A car with armour plating that may have been modified for use as a sniper "firing platform" was also discovered.
